labs.r: ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE = time-critical neurological emergency requiring CODE STROKE TEAM ACTIVATION + multidisciplinary response + rapid assessment + imaging + treatment within tight windows (tPA <4.5 hr LKW; thrombectomy <24 hr LKW for LVO). RECOGNITION + ACTIVATION + STAT WORKUP foundational. RN role: rapid assessment + IV access + labs + BP control + family communication + multidisciplinary coordination.

labs.n: NIH STROKE SCALE + STROKE WORKUP + imaging + tPA decision
labs.v: NIH STROKE SCALE (NIHSS) = standardized stroke severity assessment 0-42 (higher = more severe + worse prognosis); 11 components: (1a) LEVEL OF CONSCIOUSNESS 0-3 (alert → coma); (1b) LOC ORIENTATION questions 0-2; (1c) LOC COMMANDS 0-2; (2) BEST GAZE 0-2 (forced deviation); (3) VISUAL FIELDS 0-3 (homonymous hemianopia); (4) FACIAL PALSY 0-3 (minor → complete); (5a) MOTOR ARM L 0-4 (no drift → no movement); (5b) MOTOR ARM R 0-4; (6a) MOTOR LEG L 0-4; (6b) MOTOR LEG R 0-4; (7) LIMB ATAXIA 0-2; (8) SENSORY 0-2 (mild → severe); (9) BEST LANGUAGE 0-3 (aphasia); (10) DYSARTHRIA 0-2; (11) EXTINCTION + INATTENTION 0-2; max total 42. SEVERITY: 0-4 mild + 5-15 moderate + 16-20 moderate-severe + 21+ severe; NIHSS ≥6 indicates significant stroke; ≥10 large vessel occlusion likely + thrombectomy candidate. THIS PATIENT NIHSS 18 = moderate-severe + LVO likely + thrombectomy candidate + significant outcome benefit if reperfusion achieved. STAT NEUROIMAGING per AHA stroke guidelines: (1) CT HEAD NON-CONTRAST = first imaging; rule out ACUTE INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE (absolute contraindication to tPA + alternative management); assess EARLY ISCHEMIC CHANGES (loss of gray-white differentiation + hypoattenuation + sulcal effacement + insular ribbon sign + hyperdense MCA sign + lentiform nucleus obscuration); ASPECTS (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score) 10-point assessment of MCA territory — scores ≥6 favorable for treatment + <6 less favorable (large core infarct + lower benefit + higher hemorrhage risk); THIS PATIENT ASPECTS 8/10 favorable; (2) CTA HEAD + NECK = vascular imaging; identifies LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION (LVO) — ICA + M1 + M2 + basilar + others; required for thrombectomy planning; can also evaluate carotid + vertebral atherosclerosis + Circle of Willis; (3) CT PERFUSION (CTP) = identifies CORE INFARCT (irreversibly damaged tissue; CBV/CBF severely reduced) vs PENUMBRA (salvageable tissue with reperfusion — peripheral oligemia + hypoperfusion + delayed time-to-peak); allows EXTENDED-WINDOW selection (6-24 hr post-LKW) for thrombectomy per DAWN + DEFUSE-3 trials; favorable = small core + large penumbra (mismatch ≥1.8 + core <70 mL); THIS PATIENT favorable CTP (core 30 mL + penumbra 180 mL = mismatch ratio 6 = thrombectomy benefit anticipated); (4) MRI selected cases (more sensitive for acute infarct + posterior fossa + cervical dissection + nontraditional presentations) — diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) shows acute infarct earliest. tPA (IV ALTEPLASE) CRITERIA per AHA/ASA: ELIGIBLE = (1) clinical diagnosis of ischemic stroke; (2) measurable neurologic deficit; (3) symptom onset clearly defined + WITHIN 4.5 HR of LKW (LAST KNOWN WELL); (4) age 18+; (5) blood pressure <185/110 (treat to lower if needed); (6) no acute intracranial hemorrhage on CT; (7) no large established infarct on CT (ASPECTS ≥6); (8) no recent major surgery (<14 days) + no recent stroke (<3 months) + no recent head trauma (<3 months) + no brain tumor + no AVM + no aneurysm; (9) coagulation status acceptable (INR <1.7 + platelets >100k + no recent therapeutic anticoagulant exposure); (10) glucose >50 + no recent GI/GU bleed + multiple other specific contraindications. EXTENDED-WINDOW tPA 4.5-9 HR per EXTEND/ECASS-4 in selected patients with FAVORABLE PERFUSION IMAGING MISMATCH (DWI vs PWI mismatch on MRI or CTP); newer evidence supports treating wake-up stroke or LKW unclear if perfusion imaging favorable. ALTERNATIVE TENECTEPLASE 0.25 mg/kg IV bolus (single dose) emerging as comparable or superior to alteplase per EXTEND-IA TNK + multiple trials — simpler administration (no infusion) + may improve outcomes; gaining acceptance + some institutions now use as first-line. ALTEPLASE DOSING per AHA: 0.9 mg/kg IV (max 90 mg) = 10% IV BOLUS over 1 min + 90% INFUSION over 60 min; THIS PATIENT 80 kg × 0.9 = 72 mg = 7.2 mg bolus + 64.8 mg over 60 min. THIS PATIENT met all criteria + tPA initiated within DOOR-TO-NEEDLE 40 minutes (within ≤60 min goal; some centers achieve ≤45 or ≤30 with optimized workflow).
labs.r: NIHSS standardized assessment + STAT neuroimaging (CT head + CTA + CTP) + tPA criteria/contraindications + Door-to-Needle time critical. TENECTEPLASE emerging alternative. EXTENDED-WINDOW tPA 4.5-9 hr selected with perfusion imaging. RN role: NIHSS assessment + imaging coordination + medication administration + monitoring + family + multidisciplinary.

labs.v: BLOOD PRESSURE management for tPA eligibility + safety: (1) PRE-tPA TARGET = SBP <185 + DBP <110 (must be controlled before tPA initiation; sustained higher pressures contraindicate tPA — increased hemorrhagic transformation risk); (2) IV ANTIHYPERTENSIVES preferred (rapid onset + titratable): LABETALOL 10-20 mg IV bolus over 1-2 min (can repeat every 10-20 min; max 300 mg cumulative; CONTRAINDICATIONS = asthma + severe HF + heart block); NICARDIPINE 5 mg/hr IV infusion + titrate by 2.5 mg/hr q5-15 min (max 15 mg/hr; vasodilator + smooth response); CLEVIDIPINE 1-2 mg/hr titrated (newer + similar to nicardipine + may have faster onset/offset); HYDRALAZINE 10 mg IV q4-6h PRN (alternative + reflex tachycardia); ENALAPRILAT 0.625-1.25 mg IV (alternative + ACE inhibitor). AVOID rapid drops (more than 20% reduction in MAP can extend penumbra into infarct); REASSESS q15 min during titration; (3) POST-tPA TARGET first 24 hr = SBP <180 + DBP <105 (lower threshold to reduce hemorrhagic transformation risk; treat if exceeds + use IV antihypertensives + arterial line for continuous monitoring); after 24 hr post-tPA = standard BP goals (SBP <140 per recent evidence + AHA) + transition to oral antihypertensives. tPA ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATIONS per AHA: (1) acute intracranial hemorrhage on CT; (2) ischemic stroke or severe head trauma within 3 months; (3) acute MI within 3 months (relative); (4) intracranial neoplasm + AVM + aneurysm; (5) hypertension >185/110 unresponsive to treatment; (6) active internal bleeding (recent GI/GU bleed within 21 days; recent major surgery within 14 days); (7) bleeding diathesis (INR >1.7 + platelets <100k + recent therapeutic anticoagulant — DOAC within 48 hr or warfarin INR >1.7); (8) glucose <50 OR >400 (relative — extreme); (9) age <18; (10) extremely large established infarct (relative — ASPECTS <6 historically). RELATIVE contraindications include: NIHSS <4 or rapidly improving (consider benefit vs risk); pregnancy; recent MI; recent GI/GU bleed; recent surgery (<14 days minor + <3 months major); recent acute MI; chronic anticoagulant use (review timing + reversal); seizure at onset (need to distinguish from postictal); minor + non-disabling deficits; advanced age (no upper age limit per AHA — treat based on individual). HEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION post-tPA ~5-10% incidence; SYMPTOMATIC INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE (sICH) ~5% (worsening neuro + new hemorrhage on CT); FATAL ICH ~1-2%; TREATMENT if sICH = STOP tPA + emergent CT head + neurosurgery consult + fresh frozen plasma + cryoprecipitate + reverse antifibrinolytic; SCREENING for sICH = neurochecks q15 min × 2 hr post-tPA then q30 min × 6 hr then q1h × 16 hr (24 hr total intensive monitoring per AHA + institutional protocols). DOOR-TO-NEEDLE (DTN) TIME goal ≤60 minutes per AHA (target stroke metrics) + ≤45 min achievable + ≤30 min optimal; faster = better outcomes. THIS PATIENT BP 192/108 on arrival → labetalol 10 mg IV → BP 172/96 → additional labetalol if needed → BP 168/92 controlled <185/110 → tPA initiated; Door-to-Needle 40 minutes (within target).
labs.r: BP management for tPA: <185/110 pre-tPA + <180/105 first 24 hr post-tPA. Labetalol + nicardipine + clevidipine + hydralazine + enalaprilat options. Avoid rapid drops. tPA absolute + relative contraindications. Hemorrhagic transformation ~5-10% + sICH ~5%. Door-to-Needle ≤60 min goal. RN role: BP monitoring + medication administration + recognition + escalation.

labs.v: ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY (mechanical clot retrieval) for LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION (LVO) = transformative treatment + significantly improves outcomes; INDICATIONS per AHA/ASA: (1) anterior circulation LVO (ICA + M1 + selected M2 + selected proximal A1/A2); (2) NIHSS ≥6 (most patients; some institutions accept lower with LVO); (3) ASPECTS ≥6 favorable (lower may still benefit with extended workflow + careful selection); (4) age 18+ (no upper limit per AHA; elderly benefit + individualized); (5) modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≤1 pre-stroke (functional baseline; many institutions accept higher with individual assessment); (6) Door-to-Puncture ≤90 minutes goal + Door-to-Reperfusion ≤30 min additional. EXTENDED WINDOW (DAWN + DEFUSE-3 trials): 6-24 HOURS from LKW for LVO if FAVORABLE PERFUSION IMAGING (small core + significant penumbra mismatch); these trials extended thrombectomy benefit beyond traditional 6 hr window. THROMBECTOMY DEVICES: STENT RETRIEVER (Solitaire + Trevo + others; deploy stent in clot + retract + retrieve clot in stent); ASPIRATION CATHETERS (large-bore catheters + suction + retrieve clot); COMBINATIONS for difficult cases; experienced neurointerventionalist + technique varies. TICI (Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction) SCORE for reperfusion success: 0 = no reperfusion; 1 = penetration without distal filling; 2a = partial filling <50%; 2b = partial filling ≥50%; 3 = complete reperfusion; TICI 2b/3 considered successful reperfusion + correlates with good outcomes. ANESTHESIA = GENERAL ANESTHESIA preferred in many centers (airway protection + immobility + cooperation + safe for neurointerventionalist); some centers use CONSCIOUS SEDATION for select patients; trials mixed on outcomes (general vs conscious — both acceptable; institutional + patient factors guide). MULTIDISCIPLINARY = neurointerventionalist + neuro anesthesia + ICU + neuro RN + radiology tech + scribe + family liaison. BRIDGING THERAPY = IV tPA + endovascular thrombectomy combined; both contribute to recanalization; tPA may dissolve some clot + facilitate retrieval + improve distal microvasculature; thrombectomy retrieves residual clot + restores flow; both indicated together for LVO when patient eligible for both. NEUROINTERVENTION POST-PROCEDURE = monitor neuro status + groin site (femoral access) + bleeding + neuro recovery + neurochecks per protocol + ICU monitoring × 24 hr. COMPLICATIONS = hemorrhagic transformation (similar incidence to tPA alone; 5-10%); vessel dissection or perforation; embolization to new territory; groin hematoma + pseudoaneurysm + arteriovenous fistula; contrast nephropathy; multidisciplinary management. POST-THROMBECTOMY outcomes: ~50-60% achieve good functional outcome (mRS 0-2) vs ~25-30% with tPA alone for LVO — significant improvement; THIS PATIENT NIHSS improved from 18 → 6 → 4 + dramatic clinical response indicating successful reperfusion + favorable trajectory.
labs.r: ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY for LVO = standard treatment + significantly improves outcomes vs tPA alone; Door-to-Puncture ≤90 min + extended-window 6-24 hr per DAWN/DEFUSE-3; bridging therapy (tPA + thrombectomy) common; TICI 2b/3 successful reperfusion. RN role: pre/post-procedure care + family + monitoring + escalation.

labs.v: POST-STROKE CARE comprehensive multidisciplinary approach: (1) ICU LEVEL CARE × 24 HR post-tPA + post-thrombectomy + continuous monitoring + arterial line + IV access + Foley + cardiac monitor + pulse oximetry; (2) NEUROCHECKS q15 min × 2 hr → q30 min × 6 hr → q1h × 16 hr per AHA post-tPA protocol; assess any change in level of consciousness + NIHSS + new focal deficit + signs of cerebral edema or hemorrhagic transformation (severe headache + N/V + Cushing triad + papilledema + worsening level of consciousness); EMERGENT CT HEAD if any concerning change; (3) BP CONTROL first 24 hr <180/105 (treat with IV antihypertensives); after 24 hr standard BP goals + transition to oral; (4) ANTITHROMBOTIC HOLD × 24 HR post-tPA — NO antiplatelets/anticoagulation until repeat CT head clear at 24 hr post-tPA; HALT all anticoagulants on admission + reverse if needed (FFP + PCC + vitamin K for warfarin reversal; idarucizumab for dabigatran; andexanet alfa for FXa inhibitors); (5) DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ANY ORAL INTAKE — NPO until SLP swallow evaluation passed; aspiration pneumonia is common post-stroke + preventable; bedside swallow screen (water swallow test) initial; SLP formal evaluation; gradual diet advancement per evaluation (NPO → ice chips → puree → soft → regular); modified textures + thickened liquids if needed; nutrition support (NG/Dobhoff/PEG if persistent dysphagia + duration); (6) DVT PROPHYLAXIS — mechanical SCDs initially; LOW-DOSE HEPARIN 5000 units SC q8h or ENOXAPARIN 40 mg SC daily start at 24 hr post-tPA if no hemorrhagic transformation; reduces DVT + PE risk; (7) STRESS ULCER prophylaxis = pantoprazole 40 mg IV/PO daily; (8) SKIN PROTECTION + pressure injury prevention + Braden + q2h repositioning + pressure-redistribution mattress; (9) EARLY MOBILITY when safe + post-tPA + multidisciplinary PT/OT bedside + active assistance with ROM + transfers + ambulation; (10) BOWEL/BLADDER care + Foley assessment + reduce + bowel regimen + continence assessment + plan for retraining; (11) NUTRITION + dysphagia diet + adequate calories + protein + supplementation if needed + dietitian; (12) ASPIRATION PRECAUTIONS — HOB ≥30° + oral chlorhexidine + oral care q4h + supervised feeding + thin liquids if appropriate + thickened if dysphagia + suction available; (13) GLUCOSE management 140-180 (avoid extreme hyperglycemia which worsens stroke outcomes; avoid hypoglycemia); (14) FAMILY-CENTERED + cultural sensitivity + emotional support + chaplain + social worker. SECONDARY STROKE PREVENTION: (1) ANTIPLATELET vs ANTICOAGULATION per stroke etiology — for NON-CARDIOEMBOLIC small vessel/atherosclerotic stroke = ASPIRIN 81 mg daily + consider DAPT 90 days (aspirin + clopidogrel per CHANCE + POINT trials in minor stroke/TIA reduce recurrence) then aspirin alone; for CARDIOEMBOLIC from AFib = ANTICOAGULATION (DOAC preferred over warfarin per AHA + ARISTOTLE/RE-LY/ROCKET-AF/ENGAGE-AF/HOKUSAI-VTE — apixaban + dabigatran + rivaroxaban + edoxaban; reduces stroke 50%+ + reduces intracranial bleeding vs warfarin); apixaban 5 mg BID (or 2.5 mg BID if 2 of 3: age ≥80 + weight ≤60 kg + Cr ≥1.5; reduced dose); rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (or 15 mg if CrCl 15-50); dabigatran 150 mg BID (or 110 mg if age ≥75 + bleed risk); edoxaban 60 mg daily (or 30 mg if CrCl 15-50 + weight ≤60 kg + P-gp inhibitor); avoid in mechanical valves (use warfarin); start anticoagulation at 1-14 days post-stroke depending on infarct size + bleeding risk; THIS PATIENT = AFib new-onset + cardioembolic stroke + start apixaban 5 mg BID Day 2; (2) STATIN HIGH-INTENSITY = ATORVASTATIN 80 mg daily or ROSUVASTATIN 20-40 mg daily for atherosclerotic + LDL target <70 (SPARCL trial high-intensity statin reduces stroke recurrence; even with normal LDL in stroke); for cardioembolic strokes statin still recommended for atherosclerotic comorbidity; (3) BP OPTIMIZATION = SBP <140 (some target <130 in selected); lifestyle + ACE-I or ARB or thiazide or CCB combination; (4) DIABETES management + HbA1c <7-8 individualized; (5) LIFESTYLE = Mediterranean diet + exercise + weight management + smoking cessation + alcohol moderation; (6) CAROTID STENTING or ENDARTERECTOMY for symptomatic carotid stenosis (50-99% on side of stroke); (7) PFO (patent foramen ovale) closure for selected cryptogenic strokes; (8) SCREENING for sleep apnea + cardiovascular optimization. MULTIDISCIPLINARY POST-STROKE CARE = PT (physical therapy + gait + balance + strength + mobility) + OT (occupational therapy + ADLs + cognition + visual + perceptual) + SPEECH (language + swallowing + cognitive) + NEUROPSYCHOLOGY + RECREATIONAL + VOCATIONAL therapy + CASE MANAGEMENT + SOCIAL WORK + CHAPLAIN + family + REHABILITATION specialized (acute inpatient rehab if functional + skilled nursing facility + outpatient + home therapy + community); DRIVING evaluation when appropriate + employment planning + return to function + community reintegration; LIFELONG management + chronic disease + secondary prevention + family + community.
labs.r: POST-STROKE CARE = ICU 24 hr post-tPA + neurochecks + BP control + antithrombotic hold 24 hr + DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ORAL INTAKE + DVT prophylaxis + nutrition + skin + early mobility + multidisciplinary rehab. SECONDARY PREVENTION = appropriate antiplatelet vs anticoagulation per etiology + statin + BP + diabetes + lifestyle + carotid + multidisciplinary lifelong management.

labs.r: CODE STROKE TEAM ACTIVATION + LEADERSHIP + DELEGATION + multidisciplinary + closed-loop communication + parallel processing + standardized pathway = time-critical optimization. RN role: team activation + role execution + scribe + escalation + family + multidisciplinary.

labs.v: PERTINENT NEGATIVES: NO acute intracranial hemorrhage on CT head (tPA + thrombectomy candidate); NO recent surgery + NO recent trauma + NO bleeding diathesis + NO recent anticoagulation use (no tPA contraindications); NO acute MI/arrhythmia beyond new AFib (cardiac monitoring + troponin pending; AFib is precipitant + treated post-stroke); NO acute respiratory failure beyond intubation for thrombectomy (extubated post-procedure); NO acute mental health crisis pre-stroke; NO acute renal failure or hepatic dysfunction; NO seizure activity; NO meningismus or signs of meningitis; insurance + multidisciplinary team available + experienced (Primary Stroke Center designation); family supportive + wife is RN (medical literacy + recognized symptoms + immediate 911 call). PROTECTIVE FACTORS: WIFE recognized stroke symptoms (BE FAST mnemonic) + IMMEDIATELY called 911 (knew stroke is time-critical from RN background; this single intervention saved time + improved outcomes); LAST KNOWN WELL clearly defined at 0700 (vs uncertain LKW which limits treatment options); WITHIN 4.5 HR tPA window + within 24 hr thrombectomy window; PROMPT EMS recognition + pre-arrival hospital notification + CODE STROKE activation; RAPID ED workflow + Door-to-Needle 40 minutes (within ≤60 min goal); MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM experienced + integrated; THROMBECTOMY-CAPABLE CENTER with neurointerventionalist + interventional radiology suite; LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION amenable to thrombectomy + significant penumbra (favorable CTP) + successful TICI 2b/3 recanalization; FAMILY supportive + extended family available + insurance excellent + multidisciplinary outpatient care accessible; PATIENT pre-stroke functional baseline good (mRS likely 0-1) + decisional capacity intact pre-stroke + receptive to treatment + good prognosis with reperfusion; NEW AFib identification + appropriate anticoagulation for secondary prevention (apixaban) reduces recurrence 50%+; LIFESTYLE addressable (DM + HTN + hyperlipidemia + smoking management); cultural + spiritual support available (Catholic + chaplain) + family integration; PROMPT and successful reperfusion translates to dramatic NIHSS improvement 18 → 6 → 4 = excellent recovery trajectory.
labs.r: Despite severe initial stroke, multiple PROTECTIVE FACTORS supported excellent outcome: wife RN early recognition + immediate 911 + clear LKW + within treatment window + prompt EMS + Code Stroke + rapid workflow + experienced multidisciplinary team + thrombectomy-capable center + favorable imaging + successful reperfusion + family + insurance + good baseline. Standard ideal trajectory with comprehensive intervention + lifelong management.

steps.title: Recognize Cues
steps.sub: What matters at this acute stroke presentation?
steps.inst: Select ALL findings that are clinically + critical care significant cues requiring nursing attention.

opts.text: ACUTE LMCA ISCHEMIC STROKE with NIH STROKE SCALE 18 (severe stroke + LVO likely + thrombectomy candidate); LAST KNOWN WELL 0700 (80 min before ED arrival — WITHIN 4.5 HR tPA WINDOW); BE FAST recognition by wife (RN) + immediate 911 call; multidisciplinary CODE STROKE team activation within 10 minutes
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — recognition + time-critical activation. Each minute matters (~1.9 million neurons lost per minute). Foundation for treatment. RN role: rapid assessment + team activation + family + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: BP 192/108 on arrival requires lowering BEFORE tPA (must be <185/110); LABETALOL 10 mg IV bolus (alternative nicardipine drip + clevidipine + hydralazine + enalaprilat); avoid rapid drops (>20% MAP reduction extends penumbra into infarct); post-tPA target <180/105 × 24 hr to reduce hemorrhagic transformation risk; reassess q15 min during titration
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — BP management for tPA eligibility + safety. Standard practice. RN role: BP monitoring + medication administration + escalation.

opts.text: STAT IMAGING — CT HEAD non-contrast IMMEDIATELY (rule out hemorrhage + assess early ischemic changes ASPECTS 8/10 favorable); CTA HEAD + NECK (LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION LEFT M1 — thrombectomy candidate); CT PERFUSION (core 30 mL + penumbra 180 mL = favorable for reperfusion + thrombectomy benefit; extended-window 6-24 hr per DAWN/DEFUSE-3 if needed); MRI selected cases
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — STAT neuroimaging + treatment selection. Standard AHA protocol. RN role: imaging coordination + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: tPA CONTRAINDICATIONS reviewed — no acute hemorrhage + no recent surgery + no recent stroke + no brain tumor + no bleeding diathesis + INR 1.1 normal + platelets 220 normal + not on anticoagulant + BP controlled <185/110 + glucose 142 acceptable + age 74 (no upper limit per AHA); ELIGIBLE; consent obtained from wife (proxy) + patient with limited communication
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — tPA contraindications systematic review. Standard practice. RN role: contraindication review + medication administration + family communication.

opts.text: IV ALTEPLASE (tPA) 0.9 mg/kg × 80 kg = 72 mg = 10% IV BOLUS 7.2 mg over 1 min + 90% INFUSION 64.8 mg over 60 min; DOOR-TO-NEEDLE TIME 40 minutes (within ≤60 min AHA goal); TENECTEPLASE 0.25 mg/kg IV bolus alternative emerging as comparable or superior + simpler administration (EXTEND-IA TNK + multiple trials); BRIDGING therapy = tPA + thrombectomy combined
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — tPA administration + dosing + Door-to-Needle. Standard AHA protocol. RN role: medication preparation + administration + monitoring.

opts.text: ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY for LVO within 24 hr per AHA + DAWN/DEFUSE-3; Door-to-Puncture ≤90 min goal; TICI 2b/3 recanalization successful; stent retriever (Solitaire) + aspiration catheter; general anesthesia preferred; complications include hemorrhagic transformation + vessel dissection + groin hematoma + contrast nephropathy; significantly improves outcomes vs tPA alone for LVO
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — endovascular thrombectomy + LVO management. Standard practice + significant outcome benefit. RN role: pre/post-procedure care + family + monitoring + escalation.

opts.text: POST-tPA + POST-THROMBECTOMY ICU CARE × 24 HR: continuous monitoring + neurochecks q15 min × 2 hr → q30 min × 6 hr → q1h × 16 hr; BP target <180/105; HOLD antiplatelets/anticoagulants × 24 hr; DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ANY ORAL INTAKE (NPO until SLP swallow evaluation); DVT prophylaxis mechanical SCDs initially + heparin SC when bleeding risk acceptable; stress ulcer prophylaxis; skin + HOB ≥30° + oral care; family + chaplain + multidisciplinary
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — post-tPA ICU care + comprehensive bundle. Standard AHA protocol. RN role: monitoring + escalation + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: SECONDARY STROKE PREVENTION — APIXABAN 5 mg PO BID (DOAC for AFib — preferred over warfarin per AHA + ARISTOTLE trial; reduces stroke 50%+); ATORVASTATIN 80 mg PO daily (high-intensity statin per SPARCL trial); LISINOPRIL 10 mg PO daily (BP optimization); ASA 81 mg transitional then apixaban alone (cardioembolic stroke — no DAPT in this patient); BP target <140; diabetes management + lifestyle + smoking cessation + carotid evaluation
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — secondary stroke prevention. Standard practice. RN role: medication administration + education + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: MULTIDISCIPLINARY POST-STROKE CARE: PT (physical therapy + gait + balance + strength + mobility) + OT (ADLs + cognition + visual + perceptual) + SPEECH (language + swallowing + cognitive) + NEUROPSYCHOLOGY + RECREATIONAL/VOCATIONAL + CASE MANAGEMENT + SOCIAL WORK + CHAPLAIN + family + REHABILITATION specialized + DRIVING evaluation + lifelong management
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — multidisciplinary rehab + lifelong management. Foundation for sustained recovery + return to function. RN role: coordination + advocacy + family + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: Allergies: NKDA — document and proceed
opts.rat: Allergy documentation. No medication contraindications in current regimen. Not the priority cue but important for safety.

opts.text: ADMINISTER IV ALTEPLASE (tPA) IMMEDIATELY at NIHSS recognition WITHOUT obtaining CT head first — every minute matters + delaying for imaging wastes critical time
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG + DANGEROUS approach. CT HEAD NON-CONTRAST IS MANDATORY BEFORE tPA to RULE OUT INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE (absolute contraindication to tPA; tPA + ICH = life-threatening worsening + hemorrhage extension + death). Standard AHA protocol = STAT CT head + interpret + then tPA decision if criteria met. Skipping imaging is unacceptable + standard of care violation. RN role: ensure imaging occurs + standard pathway.

opts.text: Continue daily aspirin 81 mg post-tPA — antiplatelet provides additional stroke prevention + reduces thrombotic risk during acute period
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG approach. HOLD ALL ANTIPLATELETS/ANTICOAGULANTS × 24 HR POST-tPA — adding antiplatelet during acute post-tPA period dramatically INCREASES hemorrhagic transformation risk (~5-10% baseline; antiplatelet/anticoagulant addition during this window increases substantially); STANDARD = NO antiplatelets/anticoagulants × 24 hr post-tPA + repeat CT head clear before resuming/initiating + then start secondary prevention Day 2. AHA protocol.

steps.title: Analyze Cues
steps.sub: What stroke + tPA + thrombectomy + post-stroke principles apply?
steps.inst: Select ALL accurate linkages between cues and underlying principles.

opts.text: ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE = time-critical neurological emergency (each minute ~1.9 million neurons lost); CODE STROKE TEAM ACTIVATION within 10 min of recognition + multidisciplinary; NIH STROKE SCALE 0-42 standardized assessment + severity classification; STAT NEUROIMAGING (CT head non-contrast first + CTA head/neck + CT perfusion for extended-window selection) per AHA guidelines
opts.rat: CORRECT — stroke recognition + activation + imaging framework. Standard practice. Foundation for time-critical management.

opts.text: IV ALTEPLASE (tPA) criteria per AHA: ischemic stroke + measurable deficit + within 4.5 HR LKW + age 18+ + BP <185/110 + no hemorrhage + INR <1.7 + platelets >100k + no recent surgery/stroke/bleed/anticoagulation + multiple specific contraindications; DOSE 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg = 10% bolus + 90% infusion 60 min; TENECTEPLASE 0.25 mg/kg single bolus alternative emerging as comparable or superior
opts.rat: CORRECT — tPA criteria + dosing + alternatives framework. Standard practice. RN role: contraindication review + medication administration.

opts.text: BP MANAGEMENT for tPA: pre-tPA target <185/110 (must be controlled before initiation; sustained higher pressures contraindicate); LABETALOL 10-20 mg IV bolus + nicardipine 5 mg/hr drip + clevidipine + hydralazine + enalaprilat options; AVOID rapid drops; post-tPA target <180/105 × 24 hr to reduce hemorrhagic transformation risk; transition to standard goals after 24 hr
opts.rat: CORRECT — BP management framework. Standard practice. Foundation for tPA eligibility + safety.

opts.text: ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY for LVO per AHA + DAWN/DEFUSE-3 trials: anterior circulation LVO + NIHSS ≥6 + ASPECTS ≥6 + Door-to-Puncture ≤90 min; EXTENDED WINDOW 6-24 hr with favorable perfusion imaging; bridging therapy (tPA + thrombectomy) common; TICI 2b/3 successful reperfusion + significantly improves outcomes vs tPA alone (50-60% mRS 0-2 vs 25-30%)
opts.rat: CORRECT — thrombectomy framework + extended window. Standard practice. RN role: pre/post-procedure care + monitoring + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: POST-tPA ICU CARE × 24 HR: continuous monitoring + neurochecks q15 min × 2 hr → q30 min × 6 hr → q1h × 16 hr; BP target <180/105; HOLD antiplatelets/anticoagulants × 24 hr (5-10% hemorrhagic transformation risk; 5% symptomatic ICH); repeat CT head 24 hr post-tPA before resuming antithrombotic; multidisciplinary post-stroke care begins
opts.rat: CORRECT — post-tPA ICU care framework. Standard AHA protocol. Foundation for safety + outcome.

opts.text: DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ANY ORAL INTAKE — NPO until SLP swallow evaluation passed; aspiration pneumonia common post-stroke + preventable; bedside swallow screen by RN initial (water swallow test) + SLP formal evaluation + gradual diet advancement per evaluation (NPO → ice chips → puree → soft → regular) + modified textures + thickened liquids if needed; nutrition support; HOB ≥30° + supervised feeding + suction
opts.rat: CORRECT — dysphagia framework + aspiration prevention. Standard practice. Foundation for nutrition + safety + complications prevention.

opts.text: SECONDARY STROKE PREVENTION per AHA based on etiology: NON-CARDIOEMBOLIC (small vessel + atherosclerotic) = ASPIRIN + DAPT 90 days (POINT + CHANCE for minor stroke/TIA) then aspirin alone + statin high-intensity + BP + lifestyle + carotid intervention if indicated; CARDIOEMBOLIC (AFib + valvular) = ANTICOAGULATION (DOAC preferred over warfarin per AHA + ARISTOTLE/RE-LY/ROCKET-AF — apixaban + dabigatran + rivaroxaban + edoxaban; reduces stroke 50%+ + ICH less than warfarin) + statin + BP + lifestyle
opts.rat: CORRECT — secondary prevention framework based on etiology. Standard practice. RN role: medication administration + education + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: MULTIDISCIPLINARY POST-STROKE CARE: PT + OT + SPEECH + NEUROPSYCHOLOGY + RECREATIONAL/VOCATIONAL + CASE MANAGEMENT + SOCIAL WORK + CHAPLAIN + family + REHABILITATION specialized (acute inpatient + SNF + outpatient + home) + DRIVING evaluation + EMPLOYMENT + LIFELONG management + CULTURAL sensitivity + family integration
opts.rat: CORRECT — multidisciplinary rehab + lifelong management framework. Foundation for sustained recovery + return to function.

opts.text: Administer IV ALTEPLASE (tPA) WITHOUT obtaining CT head first to maximize neuroprotection — every minute matters + delaying for imaging wastes critical time
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG + DANGEROUS. CT HEAD NON-CONTRAST IS MANDATORY BEFORE tPA to RULE OUT INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE (absolute contraindication). Standard AHA protocol = STAT CT head + interpret + then tPA decision if criteria met. Skipping unacceptable.

opts.text: Continue daily aspirin 81 mg + apixaban post-tPA + DAPT initiation immediately to maximize secondary stroke prevention
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG. HOLD ALL ANTIPLATELETS/ANTICOAGULANTS × 24 HR POST-tPA — adding antiplatelet/anticoagulant during acute post-tPA period dramatically INCREASES hemorrhagic transformation risk. Standard practice = no antiplatelets/anticoagulants × 24 hr post-tPA + repeat CT clear + then start secondary prevention Day 2.

opts.text: WAIT 24 HOURS to assess swallow function before any treatment — aspiration is unlikely in alert patients + early assessment is too premature
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG. DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ANY ORAL INTAKE is standard post-stroke care because aspiration risk is HIGH even in alert patients (silent aspiration common). NPO until bedside swallow screen + SLP formal evaluation. Aspiration pneumonia is common post-stroke complication + preventable with appropriate dysphagia management. Standard practice + reduces mortality.

steps.title: Prioritize Hypotheses
steps.sub: Rank nursing concerns at this acute stroke presentation
steps.inst: Rank these nursing concerns from #1 (HIGHEST priority) to #5 (LOWEST).

opts.text: CODE STROKE TEAM ACTIVATION + STAT IMAGING + tPA DECISION + Door-to-Needle ≤60 min r/t NIHSS 18 + within 4.5 hr LKW + BE FAST recognition + LVO likely; ABC + IV access + STAT labs + STAT CT head/CTA/CTP + BP control + tPA contraindication review + IV alteplase 0.9 mg/kg administration
opts.rat: #1 — HIGHEST. Stroke is time-critical (~1.9 million neurons lost/min). CODE STROKE + tPA decision within ≤60 min foundation for outcome. RN role: rapid response + team activation + STAT workflow.

opts.text: ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY for LVO + Door-to-Puncture ≤90 min r/t left M1 occlusion confirmed on CTA + favorable CTP mismatch + thrombectomy candidate; bridging therapy with tPA + thrombectomy; TICI 2b/3 recanalization successful; significant outcome improvement vs tPA alone
opts.rat: #2 — HIGH. Thrombectomy significantly improves outcomes for LVO. Time-critical. Multidisciplinary. RN role: pre/post-procedure care + monitoring + family communication.

opts.text: POST-tPA + POST-THROMBECTOMY ICU CARE × 24 HR r/t continuous monitoring + neurochecks q15 min × 2 hr → q30 min × 6 hr → q1h × 16 hr; BP target <180/105; HOLD antiplatelets/anticoagulants × 24 hr; DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ANY ORAL INTAKE (NPO until SLP evaluation); DVT prophylaxis mechanical SCDs; stress ulcer prophylaxis; skin + HOB ≥30° + multidisciplinary
opts.rat: #3 — HIGH. Post-tPA ICU care + comprehensive bundle. Standard AHA protocol. Foundation for safety + outcome + complications prevention.

opts.text: SECONDARY STROKE PREVENTION + AFib Management r/t new-onset AFib + cardioembolic stroke; APIXABAN 5 mg PO BID (DOAC for AFib — preferred over warfarin per AHA + ARISTOTLE trial; reduces stroke 50%+); ATORVASTATIN 80 mg PO daily (high-intensity); LISINOPRIL 10 mg PO daily (BP optimization); diabetes management + lifestyle + smoking cessation + cardiac echo for AFib + cardioembolic source + cardiology consultation
opts.rat: #4 — Significant + ongoing. Secondary prevention foundation for sustained outcome + recurrence prevention. RN role: medication administration + education + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: Multidisciplinary Post-Stroke Care + Rehabilitation + Family-Centered Care r/t PT + OT + speech + neuropsychology + case management + social worker + chaplain (Catholic family) + rehabilitation specialized (acute inpatient + SNF + outpatient + home) + driving evaluation + cultural sensitivity + family integration + cognitive recovery + depression screening + community + lifelong management
opts.rat: #5 — Important throughout + at discharge. Comprehensive multidisciplinary rehab + lifelong management + family + community. Foundation for sustained recovery + return to function.

opts.text: CODE STROKE TEAM ACTIVATION + multidisciplinary engagement + STAT imaging (CT head non-contrast + CTA + CT perfusion) + parallel processing + Door-to-Needle ≤60 min goal + Door-to-Puncture ≤90 min goal
opts.rat: Standard AHA Code Stroke protocol. Time-critical. Multidisciplinary. RN role: team activation + STAT workflow + scribe.

opts.rat: Standard BP management for tPA. Standard practice. RN role: BP monitoring + medication administration + escalation.

opts.text: IV ALTEPLASE (tPA) 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg = 10% bolus + 90% infusion over 60 min (for 80 kg patient = 7.2 mg bolus + 64.8 mg infusion); within 4.5 hr LKW + all criteria met + contraindications excluded + consent obtained

opts.text: ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY for LVO (left M1) + favorable imaging + Door-to-Puncture ≤90 min; bridging therapy with tPA; stent retriever + aspiration catheter; general anesthesia + neurointerventionalist + interventional radiology suite; TICI 2b/3 reperfusion target

opts.text: Administer IV ALTEPLASE (tPA) WITHOUT obtaining CT head first to maximize neuroprotection — every minute matters + delaying for imaging wastes critical time
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG + DANGEROUS. CT HEAD MANDATORY BEFORE tPA to rule out intracranial hemorrhage (absolute contraindication). Standard AHA protocol = STAT CT head + then tPA. Skipping unacceptable + standard of care violation.

opts.text: Continue daily aspirin 81 mg + start apixaban immediately post-tPA + DAPT to maximize secondary stroke prevention
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG. HOLD ALL ANTIPLATELETS/ANTICOAGULANTS × 24 HR POST-tPA — adding during acute post-tPA period dramatically INCREASES hemorrhagic transformation risk. Standard practice = no antiplatelets/anticoagulants × 24 hr + repeat CT clear + then start Day 2.

opts.text: DELAY dysphagia screening for 24 hours — aspiration unlikely in alert patients + early assessment premature; allow patient to drink water and eat normally during initial 24 hours
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG. DYSPHAGIA SCREENING BEFORE ANY ORAL INTAKE is standard post-stroke care — aspiration risk HIGH even in alert patients (silent aspiration common). NPO until bedside swallow screen + SLP formal evaluation. Standard practice + reduces aspiration pneumonia + mortality.

opts.text: Initiate aggressive BP lowering to SBP <120 to maximize cerebral perfusion + prevent further infarction
opts.rat: ⚠️ WRONG approach. Aggressive BP lowering (>20% MAP reduction) extends penumbra into infarct + worsens stroke. STANDARD = pre-tPA <185/110 + post-tPA <180/105 × 24 hr + after 24 hr standard goals + gentle lowering. Maintaining adequate cerebral perfusion pressure essential.

steps.title: Take Action
steps.sub: FIRST action sequence at acute stroke presentation
steps.inst: Rank the order in which the RN should implement these actions. #1 = FIRST.

opts.text: ED 0900 (Door-to-Needle 40 min): tPA initiated + Door-to-Needle within ≤60 min goal; BP controlled to <185/110; tPA contraindications excluded; bridging thrombectomy activated; multidisciplinary team coordinated; family at bedside

RCA + just culture + system improvement + protocol education. This scenario demonstrates WHY mandatory imaging matters. NEVER skip CT before tPA.

title: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) Type II in 65-Year-Old Woman Post-Operative Day 7 from Right Total Hip Arthroplasty on Subcutaneous Heparin DVT Prophylaxis: Platelet Drop from 220 to 88 (60% Reduction) + New Right Lower Extremity DVT + 4Ts Score 7 (High Probability); STOP ALL Heparin Products Including Flushes + Initiate Direct Thrombin Inhibitor Argatroban, AVOID Warfarin Until Platelet Recovery, and AVOID Platelet Transfusion
subtitle: HEPARIN-INDUCED THROMBOCYTOPENIA (HIT) Type II = immune-mediated PROTHROMBOTIC syndrome (despite low platelets) caused by IgG antibodies against PLATELET FACTOR 4 (PF4)/HEPARIN COMPLEX → activates platelets + endothelium + monocytes → thrombosis (paradoxical — 30-75% develop thrombosis WITHOUT treatment + 5-10% mortality); INCIDENCE = ~1-5% with unfractionated heparin (UFH) + 0.1-1% with low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH); RISK FACTORS = post-cardiac surgery (highest risk + 1-3% incidence) + post-orthopedic + female + age + UFH > LMWH > fondaparinux + bovine > porcine heparin; TIMING typically 5-10 DAYS after heparin exposure (this patient POD 7); RAPID-ONSET HIT (within 24 hr) in patients with recent heparin exposure (past 100 days); DELAYED-ONSET HIT (after heparin stopped — up to 3 weeks); HIT TYPE I = non-immune + mild + transient + within 1-4 days + does not require treatment; HIT TYPE II = immune + serious + needs intervention; 4Ts SCORE = pre-test probability tool 0-8 points: (1) Thrombocytopenia — fall >50% with nadir ≥20k = 2 points; 30-50% fall = 1; <30% = 0; (2) Timing — typical 5-10 days = 2; <4 days with recent exposure = 2; <4 days no exposure = 0; >10 days = 1; (3) Thrombosis — new venous/arterial = 2; skin necrosis = 2; suspected = 1; (4) other causes — none apparent = 2; possible = 1; definite = 0; SCORE 0-3 = LOW probability (<1%; HIT unlikely; alternative diagnoses); 4-5 = INTERMEDIATE (10-30%); 6-8 = HIGH (30-80%); THIS PATIENT 4Ts = 7 = HIGH probability HIT; LABORATORY confirmation: ANTI-PF4 ELISA (sensitive ~99% but not specific ~85%; many false positives); FUNCTIONAL ASSAY (serotonin release assay SRA or heparin-induced platelet aggregation HIPA — gold standard + more specific; takes hours-days for results); SUSPECTED HIT requires IMMEDIATE action while awaiting confirmation (don't wait for confirmation if 4Ts high). MANAGEMENT: (1) IMMEDIATELY STOP ALL HEPARIN PRODUCTS = unfractionated heparin (drips + flushes + line maintenance + heparin-coated catheters) + LMWH (enoxaparin + dalteparin); EVEN HEPARIN FLUSHES contraindicated — use saline flushes; (2) START ALTERNATIVE NON-HEPARIN ANTICOAGULANT immediately even before HIT confirmation if 4Ts ≥4: ARGATROBAN (direct thrombin inhibitor — synthetic + IV continuous infusion 2 mcg/kg/min titrated to aPTT 1.5-3× baseline; renal dose adjust + caution in hepatic dysfunction — primarily hepatic clearance + lower dose 0.5-1 mcg/kg/min in liver disease; PT/INR affected so cannot guide warfarin transition by INR alone — use chromogenic factor Xa or anti-IIa) OR BIVALIRUDIN (direct thrombin inhibitor — IV + shorter half-life + preferred for cardiac surgery + renal-dose adjustment) OR FONDAPARINUX (factor Xa inhibitor — synthetic + less cross-reactivity with HIT antibodies + can be used in stable HIT after acute; SC); EMERGING DOAC alternative for stable HIT (apixaban + rivaroxaban + dabigatran) — increasingly accepted but ARGATROBAN/BIVALIRUDIN still standard for acute HIT with thrombosis; (3) AVOID WARFARIN until platelet count recovers >150k (early warfarin in HIT causes WARFARIN-INDUCED SKIN NECROSIS + microvascular thrombosis from protein C depletion + venous limb gangrene); transition to warfarin once platelets recover + overlap with argatroban × 5 days + INR target 2-3 then discontinue argatroban; (4) AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION (even with very low platelets) — counterintuitive but evidence-based; platelet transfusion in HIT can paradoxically WORSEN thrombosis by providing more substrate for activation + clot formation; only consider for life-threatening bleeding which is rare in HIT; (5) IMAGING — Doppler ultrasound for DVT + CT chest if PE suspected; CT abdomen/pelvis if abdominal symptoms; (6) DURATION of anticoagulation = at least 3 months for HIT with thrombosis (HITT) + at least 4 weeks for isolated HIT without thrombosis; (7) MEDICAL ALERT bracelet + documentation + future avoidance of heparin (lifelong avoidance for HIT antibodies typically wane but recurrence possible with re-exposure); (8) CARDIAC SURGERY in HIT patients = challenge (bivalirudin commonly used during CPB); informed consent + multidisciplinary; CONSEQUENCES of UNDETECTED HIT = paradoxical thrombosis (DVT + PE + arterial — stroke + MI + limb ischemia + skin necrosis at injection sites + adrenal hemorrhage rare); mortality 5-10% even with treatment + higher untreated

labs.v: HEPARIN-INDUCED THROMBOCYTOPENIA (HIT) TYPE II = IMMUNE-MEDIATED PROTHROMBOTIC syndrome (despite low platelets) caused by IgG antibodies against PLATELET FACTOR 4 (PF4)/HEPARIN COMPLEX → activates platelets via FcγRIIa receptor → platelet aggregation + microparticle release + endothelial activation + monocyte activation + tissue factor → THROMBOSIS (paradoxical given thrombocytopenia — counterintuitive but central to HIT); also platelet consumption + degranulation contributes to thrombocytopenia. INCIDENCE: ~1-5% with UNFRACTIONATED HEPARIN (UFH) + 0.1-1% with LOW-MOLECULAR-WEIGHT HEPARIN (LMWH — enoxaparin + dalteparin + tinzaparin; LMWH 5-10× less risk than UFH); essentially ZERO with FONDAPARINUX (synthetic factor Xa inhibitor; no PF4 cross-reactivity); RISK FACTORS = TYPE OF HEPARIN (UFH > LMWH > fondaparinux + bovine > porcine); DURATION (5-10 days typical); POPULATION (post-cardiac surgery 1-3% highest; post-orthopedic 0.5-2%; medical patients lower); SEX (female > male); AGE (elderly higher); CARDIAC SURGERY + CPB exposure higher; RECENT HEPARIN exposure within 100 days (rapid-onset HIT within 24 hr if re-exposure). TIMING typically 5-10 DAYS after heparin initiation (this patient POD 7 — typical window); RAPID-ONSET HIT within 24 hr in patients with recent heparin exposure (past 100 days; cross-reactivity); DELAYED-ONSET HIT after heparin stopped — up to 3 weeks (rare; antibodies persist + clinical deterioration). HIT TYPE I = NON-IMMUNE + transient direct heparin effect on platelets + within 1-4 days + mild (10-20% drop) + recovers without treatment + does not require alternative anticoagulant + heparin can be continued; HIT TYPE II = IMMUNE + serious + needs intervention + this patient. 4Ts SCORE = pre-test probability tool 0-8 points (Greinacher + Lo): (1) THROMBOCYTOPENIA SEVERITY — fall >50% with nadir ≥20k = 2 points; 30-50% fall OR nadir 10-19k = 1 point; <30% fall OR nadir <10k = 0; (2) TIMING — typical 5-10 days post heparin start = 2 points; <4 days with recent heparin exposure within past 100 days = 2 points; <4 days no recent exposure OR >10 days OR unclear = 0-1 point; (3) THROMBOSIS — new venous/arterial thrombosis confirmed = 2 points; skin necrosis at heparin injection sites = 2 points; suspected but not confirmed thrombosis = 1 point; no thrombosis = 0; (4) OTHER causes for thrombocytopenia — no other apparent cause = 2 points; possible alternative = 1 point; definite alternative cause = 0 points (sepsis + DIC + drug + ITP + bone marrow failure + heparin-coated catheter + post-transfusion); TOTAL SCORE 0-3 = LOW probability HIT (<5%); 4-5 = INTERMEDIATE (10-30%); 6-8 = HIGH (30-80%); HIGH 4Ts ALONE warrants empiric treatment + heparin discontinuation while awaiting confirmatory testing. THIS PATIENT 4Ts calculation: (1) Thrombocytopenia 60% fall + nadir 88 = 2 points; (2) Timing 7 days post heparin start = 2 points; (3) New DVT confirmed by Doppler = 2 points; (4) Other causes possible but heparin most likely + other causes assessed (no sepsis + no DIC + no medications other than oxycodone + no other concerning factors) = 1 point; TOTAL 4Ts = 7 (HIGH probability HIT) — empiric treatment indicated. LABORATORY CONFIRMATION: (1) ANTI-PF4 ELISA (immunoassay) — detects IgG/IgM/IgA antibodies to PF4/heparin complex; sensitive ~99% but not specific ~85% (many false positives — only IgG matters clinically + functional activity matters); positive if optical density (OD) >0.4 + strongly positive >2.0 + likely confirms HIT; (2) FUNCTIONAL ASSAY = SEROTONIN RELEASE ASSAY (SRA — gold standard + serotonin release from donor platelets exposed to patient serum + heparin) OR HEPARIN-INDUCED PLATELET AGGREGATION (HIPA — similar; less standardized); takes hours-days; more specific than ELISA + confirms clinical relevance of antibodies; positive ≥20% release of serotonin at therapeutic heparin concentration + low/no release at high heparin (heparin-dependent — characteristic of HIT); (3) WORKUP for other causes (sepsis + DIC + ITP + bone marrow failure + drug-induced + post-transfusion + heparin-coated devices) — assess for alternative explanations + treat accordingly; (4) IMAGING for thrombosis — Doppler ultrasound for DVT + CT chest if PE suspected + CT abdomen/pelvis if abdominal symptoms + cardiac imaging if cardiac source. SUSPECTED HIT requires IMMEDIATE ACTION while awaiting confirmation (don't wait for confirmation if 4Ts high — empiric treatment based on 4Ts).
labs.r: HIT TYPE II = immune-mediated prothrombotic syndrome; 4Ts SCORE 0-8 = pre-test probability; ≥6 high warrants empiric treatment; LABORATORY confirmation via anti-PF4 ELISA (sensitive + many false positives) + functional SRA/HIPA (specific gold standard). EMPIRIC TREATMENT based on 4Ts high — don't wait for laboratory confirmation if clinically suspected.

labs.n: HIT TREATMENT — STOP heparin + alternative anticoagulant + AVOID warfarin/platelets
labs.v: HIT MANAGEMENT — TIME-CRITICAL: (1) IMMEDIATELY STOP ALL HEPARIN PRODUCTS — UNFRACTIONATED HEPARIN (drips + flushes + line maintenance for arterial/central lines + heparin-coated catheters) + LMWH (enoxaparin + dalteparin + tinzaparin) + DANAPAROID (cross-reactivity); EVEN HEPARIN FLUSHES contraindicated — use SALINE FLUSHES for IV/arterial/central line maintenance; LIFETIME AVOIDANCE of heparin recommended for HIT patients (antibodies wane over months-years but can recur with re-exposure + may cause anaphylactic reaction in some); MEDICAL ALERT bracelet at discharge; (2) START ALTERNATIVE NON-HEPARIN ANTICOAGULANT IMMEDIATELY even before HIT confirmation if 4Ts ≥4: (a) ARGATROBAN — DIRECT THROMBIN INHIBITOR (DTI) synthetic small molecule; IV continuous infusion 2 mcg/kg/min (0.5-1 mcg/kg/min in hepatic dysfunction or critical illness) titrated to aPTT 1.5-3× baseline (typically 50-100 sec from baseline 30-40); RENAL CLEARANCE minimal (primarily HEPATIC clearance) — REDUCE DOSE in hepatic dysfunction + critical illness; half-life ~50 min; preferred for renal dysfunction; AFFECTS PT/INR (cannot guide warfarin transition by INR alone — use chromogenic factor Xa or anti-IIa for transition planning); HIGH-ALERT MEDICATION + 2-RN verification + barcode scanning; (b) BIVALIRUDIN — DIRECT THROMBIN INHIBITOR (DTI) peptide; IV continuous infusion 0.15-0.20 mg/kg/hr titrated to aPTT 1.5-2.5× baseline; shorter half-life ~25 min (preferred for CARDIAC SURGERY + procedures + need for rapid offset); RENAL CLEARANCE substantial — adjust for renal impairment; also affects PT/INR; (c) FONDAPARINUX — FACTOR Xa INHIBITOR synthetic + no PF4 cross-reactivity + can be used in STABLE HIT after acute treatment + outpatient; SC daily 7.5 mg (5 mg if weight <50 kg; 10 mg if >100 kg); not for acute HITT due to renal clearance + dosing constraints; (d) DOAC for STABLE HIT — RIVAROXABAN 15 mg BID × 21 days then 20 mg daily OR APIXABAN 10 mg BID × 7 days then 5 mg BID OR DABIGATRAN 150 mg BID OR EDOXABAN 60 mg daily; increasingly used for HIT + outpatient + good safety + no INR monitoring; STABLE HIT acceptable + ARGATROBAN/BIVALIRUDIN still standard for ACUTE HITT (HIT with thrombosis); (3) AVOID WARFARIN until platelets recover >150k — early warfarin in HIT depletes PROTEIN C (vitamin K-dependent + short half-life ~8 hr) BEFORE depleting prothrombotic factors → transient hypercoagulable state → WARFARIN-INDUCED SKIN NECROSIS + venous limb gangrene + microvascular thrombosis; protein C deficiency relative; AVOID warfarin in acute HIT; if patient was on warfarin pre-HIT diagnosis = reverse with vitamin K + transition to non-warfarin alternative; transition to warfarin once platelets recover + overlap with argatroban × 5 days + INR target 2-3 then discontinue argatroban; DOAC alternative simpler (no overlap needed beyond 24-48 hr); (4) AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION (even with very low platelets) — counterintuitive but evidence-based; platelet transfusion in HIT can paradoxically WORSEN thrombosis by providing more substrate for activation + clot formation; only consider for LIFE-THREATENING BLEEDING (rare in HIT — HIT is prothrombotic not bleeding); GENERALLY CONTRAINDICATED; (5) IMAGING for thrombosis — Doppler ultrasound for DVT bilaterally; CT chest if PE suspected; CT abdomen/pelvis if abdominal symptoms; cardiac imaging if cardiac source; (6) DURATION of anticoagulation = AT LEAST 3 MONTHS for HIT with thrombosis (HITT) per ACCP + multidisciplinary; AT LEAST 4 WEEKS for ISOLATED HIT without thrombosis (HIT WITHOUT THROMBOSIS — increased thrombosis risk; anticoagulation reduces; some advocate 30% develop thrombosis in following weeks if untreated); DURATION varies by clinical situation + provoking factor + risk; (7) MEDICAL ALERT bracelet + documentation in chart + family + medical home + outpatient hematology + lifetime avoidance of heparin (even heparin flushes + heparin-coated catheters + dental anesthesia with heparinized saline + caution); (8) CARDIAC SURGERY in HIT patients = challenging — BIVALIRUDIN commonly used during CPB + informed consent + multidisciplinary; ARGATROBAN during cardiac surgery less commonly used; ARGATROBAN avoided in cardiac surgery + bivalirudin preferred; PLATELET HISTORY informs management. CONSEQUENCES of UNDETECTED HIT = paradoxical thrombosis (DVT + PE + arterial — stroke + MI + limb ischemia + skin necrosis at injection sites + adrenal hemorrhage rare); mortality 5-10% even with treatment + higher untreated; significant morbidity (limb loss + amputation + organ damage). FOLLOW-UP HIT testing — anti-PF4 antibodies typically wane within 100 days (median ~50 days) + functional assay clears first; routine retesting not necessary; if re-exposure unavoidable + appropriate clinical situation = monitor closely + alternative if antibodies persist. CULTURAL + family + emotional + spiritual support throughout + transparent communication.
labs.r: HIT MANAGEMENT = (1) STOP ALL HEPARIN PRODUCTS including flushes + LIFETIME avoidance; (2) START alternative anticoagulant = ARGATROBAN (DTI; preferred renal; hepatic clearance) OR BIVALIRUDIN (DTI; preferred cardiac surgery + procedures; renal clearance) OR FONDAPARINUX (Xa inhibitor; stable HIT + outpatient) OR DOAC (stable HIT + outpatient); (3) AVOID WARFARIN until platelets recover >150k (warfarin-induced skin necrosis + venous limb gangrene from protein C depletion); (4) AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION (paradoxically worsens thrombosis); (5) IMAGING for thrombosis; (6) DURATION 3+ months HITT + 4+ weeks isolated; (7) MEDICAL ALERT bracelet + documentation + lifetime avoidance.

labs.v: ARGATROBAN administration + monitoring + transition planning: PHARMACOLOGY = DIRECT THROMBIN INHIBITOR (DTI) synthetic small molecule that binds reversibly to active site of thrombin (free + clot-bound thrombin); no antidote (unlike heparin reversed with protamine); short half-life ~50 min (so discontinuation = rapid offset); primarily HEPATIC clearance (90%) + renal 10%; well-tolerated. INDICATIONS = (1) HIT or suspected HIT; (2) HIT-associated thrombosis; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in HIT or at risk for HIT; INFUSION DOSING for HIT: 2 mcg/kg/min IV continuous infusion (initial dose for typical patient) titrated to aPTT 1.5-3× baseline (typical target 50-100 sec from baseline 30-40); REDUCED DOSE 0.5-1.2 mcg/kg/min for hepatic dysfunction (Child-Pugh B/C) + critical illness (heart failure + anasarca + post-cardiac surgery + multiorgan dysfunction); FOR PCI = bolus 350 mcg/kg followed by infusion 25 mcg/kg/min titrated. MONITORING = aPTT q2-4h initial titration → q4-6h once stable; goal 1.5-3× baseline (typically 50-100 sec); CONTROL aPTT obtained baseline before initiation; ALT/AST monitoring (hepatic clearance) + INR monitoring (impacted by argatroban — increased baseline INR ~2-3 confounds warfarin transition); PT/INR cannot guide warfarin transition by INR alone — use CHROMOGENIC FACTOR Xa or ANTI-IIa OR target INR while ON argatroban + then discontinue argatroban to assess warfarin alone. SIDE EFFECTS = BLEEDING (similar to other anticoagulants — major bleeding 7-10% + intracranial 1%); NO ANTIDOTE — supportive care + cessation + plasma transfusion (no proven efficacy) + FFP + cryoprecipitate; ELEVATED LFTs (rare); ARRHYTHMIA + hypotension (rare). TRANSITION FROM ARGATROBAN TO ORAL ANTICOAGULATION: (1) WARFARIN transition — wait until platelets recover >150k + give warfarin while continuing argatroban × 5 days minimum overlap (warfarin takes 5+ days for full effect via vitamin K-dependent factor depletion); ARGATROBAN AFFECTS INR (artificially elevates) — assess INR PRE-warfarin to establish baseline + adjust target; some institutions use CHROMOGENIC FACTOR Xa or anti-IIa for argatroban + INR for warfarin separately; STOP argatroban + recheck INR 2 hr later — target INR 2-3 sustained on warfarin alone; continue warfarin × 3 months for HITT + 4 weeks for isolated HIT; (2) DOAC TRANSITION — APIXABAN 10 mg BID × 7 days then 5 mg BID for acute DVT in HIT (this patient) OR rivaroxaban 15 mg BID × 21 days then 20 mg daily; DOACs have rapid onset (within hours) — less overlap needed than warfarin; STANDARD = start DOAC while on argatroban × 24-48 hr to ensure overlap then discontinue argatroban; SIMPLER + outpatient + no INR monitoring + no protein C depletion concern + comparable efficacy + similar bleeding risk; (3) FONDAPARINUX transition — synthetic factor Xa inhibitor; no PF4 cross-reactivity; SC daily; for STABLE HIT + outpatient. HIGH-ALERT MEDICATION = 2-RN verification + barcode scanning + smart pump hard limits + standardized order set + close monitoring + escalation if bleeding or abnormal aPTT. THIS PATIENT plan: ARGATROBAN 2 mcg/kg/min initial (no hepatic dysfunction) titrated to aPTT 78 sec (within 50-100 target); 4-6 hr aPTT monitoring; PLATELETS recovering 88 → 78 → 142 → 218 over 4 days; APIXABAN 10 mg BID × 7 days then 5 mg BID chosen over warfarin (avoiding warfarin-induced skin necrosis + protein C depletion + simpler outpatient management); argatroban-apixaban overlap × 24 hr then discontinue argatroban; total anticoagulation duration ~3 months for HITT (right DVT confirmed).
labs.r: ARGATROBAN = direct thrombin inhibitor + synthetic + hepatic clearance + short half-life + no antidote; DOSE 2 mcg/kg/min (reduce for hepatic dysfunction); aPTT q2-6h target 50-100 sec; affects INR (cannot guide warfarin transition by INR); TRANSITION to warfarin (overlap × 5 days + after platelets recover) or DOAC (overlap × 24-48 hr; simpler + outpatient); HIGH-ALERT med + 2-RN verification + barcode + smart pump.

labs.n: WARFARIN AVOIDANCE in acute HIT + DOAC transition + secondary prevention
labs.v: WARFARIN AVOIDANCE in acute HIT is CRITICAL: (1) PATHOPHYSIOLOGY = warfarin inhibits vitamin K-dependent factor synthesis (factors II, VII, IX, X + proteins C + S); ANTICOAGULANT factors C + S have SHORTER half-lives (~8 hr for C) than prothrombotic factors II + VII + IX + X (longer half-lives 24-72 hr); EARLY warfarin in HIT (when patient already PROTHROMBOTIC from HIT) DEPLETES PROTEIN C + S FIRST → transient hypercoagulable state lasting hours-days → WARFARIN-INDUCED SKIN NECROSIS (microvascular thrombosis in subcutaneous fat + skin necrosis at extremities; rare but devastating) + VENOUS LIMB GANGRENE (massive limb thrombosis + ischemia + tissue loss + amputation risk) + MORTALITY; (2) AVOID warfarin until platelet count recovers ≥150k (typically 5-14 days after stopping heparin + appropriate alternative anticoagulant); PROTEIN C levels normalize when full anticoagulation established with non-warfarin agent + platelet recovery; (3) IF PATIENT WAS ON WARFARIN PRE-HIT diagnosis → reverse with VITAMIN K + transition to non-warfarin alternative (argatroban or bivalirudin) immediately; (4) TRANSITION to warfarin (when appropriate): platelets ≥150k + on argatroban + overlap × 5 days minimum + warfarin starting dose typical (5 mg daily) + monitor INR + ARGATROBAN affects INR artificially (elevates) — use chromogenic factor Xa or anti-IIa for argatroban + INR for warfarin separately + STOP argatroban + recheck INR 2 hr later — target INR 2-3 sustained on warfarin alone; continue warfarin × 3 months for HITT + 4 weeks for isolated HIT; (5) DOAC ALTERNATIVE (this patient — apixaban) = preferred over warfarin in many HIT patients due to: (a) no protein C depletion concern (DOACs do not affect protein C); (b) rapid onset (full anticoagulation within hours; less argatroban overlap needed); (c) no INR monitoring (simpler outpatient + medication adherence); (d) comparable efficacy + similar bleeding risk; (e) no significant drug interactions with most medications; (f) no dietary interactions (unlike warfarin + vitamin K foods); (6) DURATION = 3+ months for HIT with thrombosis (HITT) per ACCP guidelines; 4+ weeks for isolated HIT without thrombosis; longer if unprovoked or persistent risk factors; (7) FOLLOW-UP outpatient hematology + monitoring; recurrent HIT testing typically not needed (antibodies wane); medical alert bracelet + lifetime heparin avoidance; family + community + insurance + multidisciplinary; (8) ADHERENCE counseling + bleeding precautions + medical alert + dental + procedures + medication interactions + family education + emergency plan. THIS PATIENT: APIXABAN 10 mg PO BID × 7 days then 5 mg BID chosen for: (a) acute DVT treatment standard dose; (b) avoid warfarin-induced skin necrosis + venous limb gangrene; (c) no protein C depletion concern; (d) simpler outpatient management + no INR monitoring; (e) preferred DOAC for orthopedic surgery patient (vs rivaroxaban 15 mg BID × 21 days then 20 mg daily acceptable alternative); (f) family + adherence excellent + supportive; (g) Mediterranean diet + lifestyle continued; ARGATROBAN-APIXABAN OVERLAP × 24-48 hr to ensure transition + then discontinue argatroban + outpatient apixaban × 3 months total duration for HITT. MEDICAL ALERT bracelet ordered + lifetime heparin avoidance documented + outpatient hematology + orthopedic follow-up + PCP + community + family education.
labs.r: WARFARIN AVOIDANCE in acute HIT critical (warfarin-induced skin necrosis + venous limb gangrene from protein C depletion); transition to warfarin or DOAC after platelets recover ≥150k + appropriate alternative anticoagulant + appropriate overlap. DOACs preferred over warfarin in many HIT patients (no protein C depletion + rapid onset + simpler outpatient).

labs.v: PLATELET TRANSFUSION AVOIDANCE in HIT is COUNTERINTUITIVE but evidence-based: (1) HIT IS PROTHROMBOTIC despite low platelets — patient is at HIGH RISK FOR THROMBOSIS (30-75% develop thrombosis without treatment) NOT BLEEDING; bleeding is rare in HIT (the thrombosis is the main concern); (2) PLATELET TRANSFUSION in HIT can PARADOXICALLY WORSEN THROMBOSIS by providing more substrate for activation + clot formation + extending existing thrombosis or precipitating new thrombosis; multiple case reports of platelet transfusion in HIT precipitating PE + DVT + arterial thrombosis + worsening outcomes; (3) GENERAL CONTRAINDICATION to platelet transfusion in HIT EVEN WITH VERY LOW PLATELET COUNTS; (4) EXCEPTIONS = LIFE-THREATENING BLEEDING (rare in HIT) — only situation where platelet transfusion may be considered + multidisciplinary discussion + careful risk-benefit + escalation to hematology; (5) ALTERNATIVE BLEEDING MANAGEMENT in HIT — control bleeding source + supportive care + appropriate anticoagulant reversal (no proven antidote for argatroban — supportive care + FFP/cryoprecipitate may help); (6) BLEEDING PRECAUTIONS during HIT treatment — bleeding risk on argatroban similar to other anticoagulants; monitor for bleeding signs (hematemesis + melena + hematuria + nosebleeds + hematomas + skin bruising); reduce/discontinue argatroban if bleeding + reverse with FFP + supportive care; (7) PROCEDURES + invasive procedures in HIT — delay non-urgent procedures until platelet recovery + INR/aPTT acceptable; HIT patients can have procedures with appropriate anticoagulant management + bridging + multidisciplinary; (8) MEDICAL ALERT bracelet + LIFETIME heparin avoidance + future medical encounters including dental + procedures + emergency situations + family + community awareness. THIS PATIENT: NO platelet transfusion despite low platelets 88 at admission (counterintuitive but correct — patient is prothrombotic + HIT is treated with anticoagulation not platelet transfusion); MONITOR for any bleeding signs (rare in HIT); argatroban titrated to aPTT 50-100 sec + close monitoring; no procedures planned during acute phase; PLATELETS recovered 88 → 78 → 142 → 218 over 4 days (typical pattern as antibodies wane); ANTICOAGULATION maintained throughout per HIT management. CULTURAL + family + spiritual + emotional support throughout (Chinese-American + bilingual home + Buddhist + chaplain coordinated with Buddhist chaplain).
labs.r: PLATELET TRANSFUSION AVOIDANCE in HIT is critical + counterintuitive but evidence-based — paradoxically worsens thrombosis. Exception = life-threatening bleeding (rare). Bleeding precautions on argatroban + appropriate management. MONITOR for thrombosis + bleeding throughout. RN role: education + advocacy + monitoring + family education.

labs.v: PERTINENT NEGATIVES: NO pulmonary embolism (no chest pain + no SOB + no tachycardia + no hypoxemia + no signs of PE); NO arterial thrombosis (no stroke + no MI + no limb ischemia + no skin necrosis at heparin injection sites); NO bleeding complications (no hematuria + no melena + no nosebleeds + no hematomas + no excessive bruising; rare in HIT); NO sepsis (no fever beyond mild + no concerning signs + no positive cultures); NO DIC (coags normal + fibrinogen preserved + no schistocytes + no organ dysfunction beyond DVT); NO ITP (no other cause for thrombocytopenia identified — heparin is most likely + 4Ts high + HIT testing positive); NO adrenal hemorrhage (no abdominal pain + no hypotension + no electrolyte abnormality); NO concurrent active malignancy (remote breast cancer in remission 8 yr ago — annual surveillance + no current malignancy); NO platelet transfusion needed (HIT prothrombotic + AVOID platelet transfusion); NO warfarin initiation acutely (avoiding warfarin-induced skin necrosis + protein C depletion); NO hepatic dysfunction (LFTs normal — appropriate argatroban dosing without adjustment); NO renal dysfunction (Cr 0.9 normal — minimal argatroban renal clearance + appropriate dosing); insurance + multidisciplinary team available + experienced; family supportive + receptive + bilingual + cultural sensitivity. PROTECTIVE FACTORS: RAPID RECOGNITION at POD 7 routine labs + platelet decline pattern + new DVT trigger workup; 4Ts SCORE 7 (HIGH) prompted immediate empiric treatment + multidisciplinary engagement; ANTIBODY TESTING POSITIVE confirming HIT diagnosis (anti-PF4 ELISA + functional SRA both positive); ARGATROBAN INITIATED IMMEDIATELY at recognition + appropriate dosing + aPTT monitoring + therapeutic range; HEPARIN STOPPED COMPLETELY (including flushes) + saline flushes substituted + lifetime heparin avoidance planned; AVOIDED WARFARIN initially (preventing warfarin-induced skin necrosis); AVOIDED PLATELET TRANSFUSION despite low platelets (paradoxical worsening prevention); DOAC TRANSITION to APIXABAN (preferred over warfarin in HIT + simpler outpatient + no INR + no protein C depletion); PATIENT RESPONSIVE to argatroban (platelets recovered + DVT improving + no progression + no new thrombosis); FAMILY supportive + extended family available + insurance excellent + multidisciplinary outpatient care accessible; CULTURAL + SPIRITUAL support (Chinese-American + Buddhist + chaplain) + family integration + interpreter services if needed (English-fluent here); MEDICAL ALERT bracelet ordered + lifetime heparin avoidance documented + medication reconciliation + outpatient hematology follow-up; PATIENT receptive + motivated + grateful + recovering well; HIP REPLACEMENT recovery on track despite HIT complication. STANDARD expected positive trajectory with comprehensive intervention + recovery from both HIT + hip replacement + lifetime heparin avoidance for prevention.
labs.r: Despite serious HIT complication, multiple PROTECTIVE FACTORS supported recovery: rapid recognition + 4Ts assessment + empiric treatment + appropriate alternative anticoagulant + warfarin avoidance + platelet transfusion avoidance + DOAC transition + multidisciplinary + family + insurance + cultural sensitivity. Standard expected positive trajectory with comprehensive intervention + lifetime heparin avoidance.

steps.title: Recognize Cues
steps.sub: What matters at this HIT recognition?
steps.inst: Select ALL findings that are clinically significant cues requiring nursing attention.

opts.text: HEPARIN-INDUCED THROMBOCYTOPENIA (HIT) Type II = immune-mediated PROTHROMBOTIC syndrome (despite low platelets) caused by IgG antibodies against PF4/heparin complex → activates platelets + thrombosis; 30-75% develop thrombosis without treatment + 5-10% mortality; incidence ~1-5% with UFH + 0.1-1% with LMWH; this patient on UFH 5000 units q8h × 7 days = at risk; timing 5-10 days typical (this patient POD 7); risk factors = post-orthopedic + female + age
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — HIT pathophysiology + epidemiology + risk factors. Foundation for recognition + treatment. RN role: recognition + escalation + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: 4Ts SCORE pre-test probability (0-8 points): (1) THROMBOCYTOPENIA SEVERITY — fall >50% with nadir ≥20k = 2 points; (2) TIMING — typical 5-10 days = 2 points; (3) THROMBOSIS — new venous/arterial = 2 points; (4) OTHER CAUSES — none apparent = 2 points; 0-3 LOW + 4-5 INTERMEDIATE + 6-8 HIGH; this patient 4Ts = 7 (HIGH probability HIT) — empiric treatment indicated without waiting for laboratory confirmation
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — 4Ts pre-test probability tool. Standard practice. RN role: assessment + escalation.

opts.text: STOP ALL HEPARIN PRODUCTS IMMEDIATELY at HIT recognition — UFH (drips + flushes + line maintenance) + LMWH (enoxaparin + dalteparin) + heparin-coated catheters + heparin-bonded devices; EVEN HEPARIN FLUSHES contraindicated — use SALINE flushes; LIFETIME HEPARIN AVOIDANCE (antibodies wane but may recur with re-exposure + medical alert bracelet)
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — heparin discontinuation including flushes + lifetime avoidance. RN role: ensure heparin completely stopped + saline flushes + medical alert + documentation.

opts.text: START ALTERNATIVE NON-HEPARIN ANTICOAGULANT immediately even before HIT confirmation if 4Ts ≥4: ARGATROBAN (DIRECT THROMBIN INHIBITOR — IV continuous 2 mcg/kg/min titrated to aPTT 1.5-3× baseline; primarily hepatic clearance + caution in liver disease + half-life 50 min) OR BIVALIRUDIN (DTI; renal clearance + preferred for cardiac surgery) OR FONDAPARINUX (factor Xa inhibitor; stable HIT + outpatient) OR DOAC (apixaban + rivaroxaban + dabigatran for stable HIT)
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — alternative anticoagulant initiation + selection. RN role: medication administration + monitoring + escalation.

opts.text: AVOID WARFARIN until platelet count recovers ≥150k — warfarin-induced SKIN NECROSIS + venous limb gangrene from PROTEIN C depletion (protein C half-life 8 hr; depleted before prothrombotic factors → transient hypercoagulable state); transition to warfarin once platelets recover + overlap with argatroban × 5 days; DOAC alternative simpler + preferred in many HIT patients (no protein C depletion + rapid onset + no INR monitoring + comparable efficacy)
opts.rat: PRIORITY CUE — warfarin avoidance in acute HIT. Standard practice. RN role: medication management + advocacy + multidisciplinary.

opts.text: AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION even with very low platelets — counterintuitive but evidence-based; platelet transfusion in HIT paradoxically WORSENS thrombosis by providing more substrate for activation + clot formation; only consider for LIFE-THREATENING BLEEDING (rare in HIT — HIT is PROTHROMBOTIC not bleeding); standard contraindication

title: Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) in 42-Year-Old Man with 4 Weeks of Productive Cough + Hemoptysis + Drenching Night Sweats + 6 kg Unintentional Weight Loss + Low-Grade Fevers: AFB Smear-Positive Sputum + Cavitary Right Upper Lobe Infiltrate on Chest X-Ray; Immediate AIRBORNE Isolation in Negative-Pressure Room + N95/PAPR Respiratory Protection + Initiation of RIPE Four-Drug Therapy (Rifampin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol), Directly Observed Therapy (DOT), Mandatory Public Health Reporting, and Contact Investigation
subtitle: ACTIVE PULMONARY TUBERCULOSIS = airborne infection caused by MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (acid-fast bacillus); TRANSMISSION via AIRBORNE DROPLET NUCLEI (1-5 micron particles that remain suspended in air for hours + travel on air currents) generated when person with active pulmonary/laryngeal TB coughs/sneezes/sings/speaks; NOT spread by fomites/surfaces/sharing utensils/touching (unlike contact-spread organisms) — this distinction drives isolation type; PATHOGENESIS = inhalation → alveolar macrophage ingestion → most contained as LATENT TB INFECTION (LTBI — granuloma + dormant bacilli + NOT infectious + asymptomatic + positive TST/IGRA + normal CXR or only calcified granuloma); REACTIVATION (or progressive primary) → ACTIVE TB (infectious + symptomatic + abnormal CXR); LIFETIME reactivation risk ~5-10% for immunocompetent + much higher with HIV/immunosuppression/TNF-inhibitors/diabetes/silicosis/renal failure/malnutrition; RISK FACTORS for exposure/infection = birth or residence in high-incidence country (Asia + Africa + Eastern Europe + Latin America) + close contact with active case + congregate settings (homeless shelters + correctional facilities + long-term care + healthcare) + healthcare workers; CLASSIC SYMPTOMS of active pulmonary TB = COUGH >2-3 weeks (initially dry then productive) + HEMOPTYSIS + drenching NIGHT SWEATS + unintentional WEIGHT LOSS + anorexia + fatigue + low-grade FEVER + pleuritic chest pain; EXTRAPULMONARY TB (lymphatic + pleural + skeletal/Pott disease + genitourinary + miliary/disseminated + meningeal + pericardial) more common with HIV. DIAGNOSIS: (1) AFB SPUTUM SMEAR (3 specimens collected 8-24 hr apart, ≥1 early-morning; acid-fast stain = rapid + indicates burden + infectiousness but does not distinguish M. tuberculosis from non-tuberculous mycobacteria); (2) NUCLEIC ACID AMPLIFICATION TEST (NAAT — e.g., Xpert MTB/RIF; rapid + confirms M. tuberculosis + detects rifampin resistance); (3) MYCOBACTERIAL CULTURE (gold standard + most sensitive + takes 2-6 weeks + provides drug-susceptibility testing — essential for resistance); (4) CHEST X-RAY (classic = upper lobe infiltrate + CAVITATION + reactivation pattern; primary TB = lower/middle lobe + hilar adenopathy + effusion; miliary = diffuse millet-seed nodules); (5) TST (tuberculin skin test — Mantoux PPD intradermal + read 48-72 hr + induration measured not erythema; cutoffs 5/10/15 mm by risk; indicates infection NOT active disease) OR IGRA (interferon-gamma release assay — QuantiFERON/T-SPOT; blood test + not affected by prior BCG vaccination + indicates infection NOT active disease); LATENT vs ACTIVE distinction critical (LTBI = positive TST/IGRA + asymptomatic + normal CXR + non-infectious + treat to prevent reactivation; ACTIVE = symptoms + abnormal CXR + positive smear/culture + infectious + treat to cure + isolate). INFECTION CONTROL: (1) AIRBORNE PRECAUTIONS immediately for suspected/confirmed active pulmonary or laryngeal TB — AIRBORNE INFECTION ISOLATION ROOM (AIIR) = NEGATIVE PRESSURE relative to hallway (air flows INTO room) + minimum 6-12 air changes per hour (ACH) + air exhausted directly outside OR through HEPA filtration before recirculation + door kept CLOSED; (2) RESPIRATORY PROTECTION = fit-tested N95 RESPIRATOR (or PAPR — powered air-purifying respirator) for all staff/visitors entering room; SURGICAL MASK is NOT adequate respiratory protection for staff (surgical mask filters large droplets not droplet nuclei) — surgical mask is placed on the PATIENT when transport is unavoidable (source control) + N95 protects the wearer; (3) MINIMIZE TRANSPORT — keep patient in room; if transport essential, patient wears SURGICAL MASK + schedule to minimize exposure; (4) PATIENT EDUCATION on cough etiquette + covering mouth + tissue disposal; (5) staff TB screening + post-exposure follow-up. PHARMACOLOGIC TREATMENT (drug-susceptible active TB): RIPE four-drug regimen for INTENSIVE PHASE × 2 months = RIFAMPIN (R; turns body fluids ORANGE-RED — urine/sweat/tears/contact lenses + induces hepatic CYP450 → many drug interactions including reduced oral contraceptive + warfarin + methadone efficacy + hepatotoxicity) + ISONIAZID (INH/H; hepatotoxicity + PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY prevented with PYRIDOXINE/vitamin B6 supplementation + drug-induced lupus) + PYRAZINAMIDE (PZA/Z; hepatotoxicity + HYPERURICEMIA/gout flare) + ETHAMBUTOL (EMB/E; OPTIC NEURITIS → monitor visual acuity + red-green color discrimination; renally cleared); followed by CONTINUATION PHASE × 4 months = RIFAMPIN + ISONIAZID (total 6 months for drug-susceptible pulmonary TB; longer for cavitary + positive 2-month culture + extrapulmonary + drug resistance); DRUG-RESISTANT TB (MDR-TB = resistant to ≥ INH + rifampin; XDR-TB = additionally resistant to fluoroquinolone + injectable/bedaquiline) requires prolonged multi-drug regimens (bedaquiline + linezolid + fluoroquinolones + others) + expert consultation. MONITORING: baseline + periodic LFTs (all three of INH/RIF/PZA hepatotoxic — hold if ALT >3× ULN with symptoms or >5× ULN asymptomatic) + visual acuity/color (ethambutol) + uric acid + adherence; DIRECTLY OBSERVED THERAPY (DOT) = standard of care to ensure adherence + prevent resistance + public health worker watches patient swallow each dose. PUBLIC HEALTH: TB is a MANDATORY REPORTABLE DISEASE — notify local/state public health department; CONTACT INVESTIGATION (identify + test + treat close contacts — concentric-circle approach starting with closest/highest-exposure); DOT coordination; INFECTIOUSNESS resolves after ~2 weeks of effective therapy + clinical improvement + 3 consecutive negative AFB smears (criteria for releasing from airborne isolation/discharge home with continued therapy). HEALTH PROMOTION: screening high-risk populations + LTBI treatment to prevent active disease + immigrant/refugee screening + congregate-setting screening + healthcare worker screening + BCG vaccine context (used in high-incidence countries; limited efficacy in adults; causes false-positive TST → use IGRA) + community education + social determinants (housing + nutrition + access). CONSEQUENCES of undiagnosed/untreated active TB = ongoing transmission (each untreated case infects ~10-15 contacts/year) + progressive lung destruction + respiratory failure + dissemination + death (untreated active TB mortality ~50%); drug resistance from non-adherence/inadequate regimens
